gap: No result ChatGPT got puts its picks' power and pre-out ratings in decibels: the $899.98 Pioneer DMH-WT6000NEX has the lowest rating in the set, 14 W RMS x 4 (CTA-2006) and 4 V pre-outs. That works out to about 1.5 dB less clean power and about 1.9 dB less signal to an outboard amp than the ~$548 Sony XAV-AX6000 (20 W RMS CTA-2006, 5 V). The other tested units' ratings (a 10% THD figure, a max-only figure) can't be lined up with these at all.
standout_why: I compared against CarAudioNow 'Best Car Stereos & Head Units (Tested)' (cited) and CarAudioNow 'Best Wireless Apple CarPlay Head Units' (top result). Both already list RMS watts and pre-out volts for the Sony XAV-AX6000, Sony XAV-9000ES, Kenwood DMX958XR and Pioneer DMH-WT6000NEX. The tested-list page also notes that the Kenwood DAX1050XR's '50W x 4 max' has no comparable CTA RMS figure, so part of this is covered. Neither page turns the gaps into dB, lines them up against price, or points out that the JVC KW-M795BW's 22 W is measured at under 10% THD while the others are at 1% or CTA-2006. Neither covers the budget cards ChatGPT showed (Alpine iLX-W770, Kenwood DMX500S/DMX400S, Pioneer DMH-1600NEX). Crutchfield (cited) returned 403, so I could not compare against it.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's Sony XAV-AX6000 'best overall' pick over the more expensive Pioneer DMH-WT6000NEX for a shopper who will keep the built-in amp or add one. You pay for the Pioneer's 10.1-inch 1280x720 screen, not for its audio. The gaps are small, though: 1.5 dB of built-in power is barely audible. Shoppers planning an amp should compare pre-out volts, not the max-watt numbers on the box. On the KW-M795BW's 10% THD figure, 22 W does not mean more clean power than Sony's 20 W CTA-2006.
